ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — MOCK EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

2. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

3. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. blue
   D. run

4. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

5. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.

6. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. No full stops
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

7. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

8. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only an action

9. When practising Language Welcome and, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Language Welcome and.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Language Welcome and.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Language Welcome and.

10. When practising Language School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Language School.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Language School.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Language School.

11. When practising Pre Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pre Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pre Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Pre Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.

12. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. goes
   C. goed
   D. went

13. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.

14. When practising Phonics, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Phonics.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Phonics.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Phonics.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.

15. When practising Pre-Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Pre-Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-Writing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Pre-Writing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Pre-Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Handwriting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Attentive listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Language Welcome and and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Language School and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
